newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds follow German bunds higher.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds follow German bunds higher.

text.p: Irish government bonds strengthened in thin late trade on Wednesday, largely in line with Germany as the market awaited Thursday's release of the German December employment report, dealers said.
Traders said the German bond market was increasingly coming to the conclusion that Thursday's jobless data would show a rise of 60,000, above expectations of only a couple of days earlier.
The speculation on unemployment, combined with stronger U.S. Treasuries had lifted German bunds in afternoon trade, they added.
"Most of what is going on is going on internationally. We have moved pretty much with Germany, although, we have lagged bunds a small bit," one Dublin-based dealer said.

"It's hard to know what to expect from German data these days. One set of data shows the German economy is very strong and the next hints that Germany won't meet the deficit criteria for EMU," the dealer added.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had risen 20 pence from Tuesday's close to 100.75 to yield 6.29 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 25 pence to 107.75 to yield 6.86 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading 94 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 179 basis points over Germany in the five-year area.
The market awaited the release of key non-farm payrolls data from the U.S. on Friday, dealers added.
